The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 ("Cr.P.C") has been filed by the petitioners praying for quashing of FIR bearing no. 385/2013 registered at Police Station Prashant Vihar, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 ("IPC") and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. Issue notice.
Ms. Richa Dhawan, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.
3. Petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr. Abhishekh Bhardwaj and Investigating Officer (IO) from Police Station Prashant Vihar, Delhi.
4. Brief facts of the present case are that petitioner no. 1 got married to respondent no. 2 on 06.05.2011 according to Hindu Rites and Customs.

On the complaint of respondent no.2, an FIR bearing no. 385/2013 was registered at Police Station Prashant Vihar, Delhi for the offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of IPC against the petitioners.

It is stated both the parties have settled all their disputes vide Settlement Deed dated 14.10.2022.
5.

On a query made by this Court, respondent no. 2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any Nitin Suri & Anr vs State Of Nct Of Delhi & Anr on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79319777/
1 pressure, coercion or threat.

sentences.text:
It is also stated by respondent no. 2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties vide Settlement Deed dated 14.10.2022 and learned counsel for the petitioners submitted affidavit showing the protection of interest of minor child as per the judgment titled as Ganesh vs. Sudhirkumar Shrivastava, (2020) 20 SCC 787 passed by the Honble Supreme Court have been filed and the same are on record.
6.

It is submitted that respondent no. 2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner no. 1 and other family members.

7. The petitioner no. 1 had paid a sum of Rs. 35,00,000/- in two installments in the following manner:
a. First installment of Rs. 20 Lakhs paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of hearing application of petitioner no. 2 for release of his passport and permission to fly back to Australia.
b. Second/Final instalment of Rs. 15 lakhs to be paid at the time of quashing of the FIR before the Honble High Court at New Delhi.
8.

Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received the last and final instalment of Rs. 15 Lacs today, i.e., 17.01.2023 vide DD No. 672653 drawn on State Bank of India,
New Delhi and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

9. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

10. Accordingly, FIR bearing no. 385/2013 registered at Police Station Prashant Vihar, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
11. The present petition stands disposed of along with pending applications.
12. The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
SWARANA KANTA SHARMA, J JANUARY 17, 2023/
